national.title: How to Transfer Vehicle RC Ownership After Buying a Used Vehicle (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step guide to transferring vehicle registration certificate ownership on the Parivahan Vahan portal. Verified statutory fees under CMVR Rule 81, Form 29 and 30 rules, and required seller documents.

steps.title: Check Pending E-Challans and Active Bank Loans
steps.description: Visit echallan.parivahan.gov.in to verify that no pending traffic fines exist. Ensure the seller provides a bank NOC if a loan was active.
steps.calloutText: Any unpaid traffic challan will freeze the vehicle record and prevent transfer approval.

steps.title: Collect Form 29 and Form 30 Signed by Seller
steps.description: Get two copies of Form 29 and two copies of Form 30 signed by the registered seller. Take a clean chassis pencil print.
steps.calloutText: Trace the chassis number using an HB pencil on the corner of both forms.

steps.title: Open Parivahan Vahan and Select State
steps.description: Visit vahan.parivahan.gov.in and select your state transport department. Enter the vehicle registration number and proceed to vehicle services.

steps.title: Select Transfer of Ownership Service
steps.description: Click on 'Apply for Transfer of Ownership' under online vehicle services. Enter the last five digits of the chassis number.

steps.title: Enter Buyer Details and Mobile Number
steps.description: Fill in the buyer's full name, father's name, present residential address, and mobile number. Generate and submit the OTP sent to buyer.

steps.title: Upload Signed Forms and Supporting Documents
steps.description: Upload scanned copies of Form 29, Form 30, valid insurance, valid PUC, and buyer address proof in PDF format.
steps.calloutText: Ensure each PDF file size is under 200 KB and clearly legible.

steps.title: Pay Statutory Government Transfer Fees Online
steps.description: Pay the transfer fee and smart card fee through the integrated government treasury payment gateway. Download the fee receipt with application number.

steps.title: Submit Physical File to RTO or Await Faceless Approval
steps.description: In faceless states, approval happens automatically online. In other states, submit original RC and signed forms to the jurisdictional RTO.
steps.where: Jurisdictional RTO Office or Speed Post Delivery

documentRequirements.name: Original Vehicle Registration Certificate (RC)
documentRequirements.description: Physical smart card or paper booklet registration certificate issued in the seller's name.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Original smart card or RC booklet

documentRequirements.name: Form 29 Notice of Transfer of Ownership
documentRequirements.description: Statutory notice of ownership transfer signed in duplicate by the registered vehicle seller.

documentRequirements.name: Form 30 Application for Transfer of Ownership
documentRequirements.description: Statutory application for intimation and transfer of ownership signed by both seller and buyer in duplicate.

documentRequirements.name: Valid Motor Vehicle Insurance Certificate
documentRequirements.description: Active third-party or comprehensive motor vehicle insurance policy valid for at least thirty days.

documentRequirements.name: Valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) Certificate
documentRequirements.description: Valid computerized emissions certificate issued by an authorized government testing centre.

documentRequirements.name: Form 35 Loan Hypothecation Termination Certificate
documentRequirements.description: NOC letter from the financing bank along with two copies of Form 35 signed by the financier.

documentRequirements.name: Form 28 No Objection Certificate (NOC)
documentRequirements.description: Three copies of Form 28 issued by the parent RTO if moving to a different RTO district or state.

documentRequirements.name: Proof of Buyer Residential Address
documentRequirements.description: Aadhaar Card, voter ID card, electricity bill, or registered rent agreement of the buyer.

rejectionReasons.title: Active Bank Hypothecation Without Form 35
rejectionReasons.description: Submitting the transfer application while the vehicle still shows a financier lien blocks RTO approval.
rejectionReasons.solution: Obtain a bank NOC and signed Form 35 from the financing bank before applying.

rejectionReasons.title: Pending Traffic E-Challans on Vehicle Number
rejectionReasons.description: Unpaid traffic violation challans recorded on the national portal prevent ownership transfer processing.
rejectionReasons.solution: Pay all pending e-challans on echallan.parivahan.gov.in before filing Form 29 and 30.

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Seller Signature or Signature Mismatch
rejectionReasons.description: If the seller's signature on Form 29 differs from original RTO records, the scrutiny clerk rejects it.
rejectionReasons.solution: Ensure the seller signs exactly as recorded in their official identity documents.

rejectionReasons.title: Expired Vehicle Insurance or PUC Certificate
rejectionReasons.description: The Motor Vehicles Act strictly prohibits ownership transfer without active insurance and valid emission certificate.
rejectionReasons.solution: Renew the insurance policy and get a fresh PUC before initiating the transfer application.

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Inter-State RTO NOC (Form 28)
rejectionReasons.description: Buying a vehicle registered in another district or state requires a clearance NOC from the original RTO.
rejectionReasons.solution: Apply for Form 28 NOC at the seller's home RTO before applying for transfer in your district.

rejectionReasons.title: Illegible Chassis Number Pencil Tracing
rejectionReasons.description: A blurry or missing physical pencil tracing of the chassis number on Form 29 delays verification.
rejectionReasons.solution: Rub an HB pencil over plain white paper firmly against the embossed chassis plate on the vehicle frame.

faqItems.question: Within how many days must an RC transfer be completed after buying a used vehicle?
faqItems.answer: The buyer must report the transfer within 30 days for local sales and 45 days for inter-state purchases.

faqItems.question: Can the seller be held liable if the buyer does not transfer the RC?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The registered owner remains legally liable for accidents and traffic fines until the RC transfer is endorsed.

faqItems.question: What is the statutory government fee to transfer a two-wheeler RC?
faqItems.answer: The statutory fee is ₹150 for ownership transfer plus ₹200 for the new smart card RC, totaling ₹350.

faqItems.question: What is the government fee to transfer ownership of a four-wheeler car?
faqItems.answer: The statutory fee is ₹300 for car ownership transfer plus ₹200 for the smart card RC, totaling ₹500.

faqItems.question: Is a police clearance certificate required for vehicle RC transfer?
faqItems.answer: No general police certificate is required. However, the RTO portal automatically verifies that the vehicle is not reported stolen.

faqItems.question: Can I transfer vehicle RC online without visiting the RTO?
faqItems.answer: Several states allow faceless transfer using Aadhaar authentication. However, some RTOs still require physical submission of Form 29 and 30.

faqItems.question: What is an NOC (Form 28) and when is it needed?
faqItems.answer: Form 28 is required when the buyer resides in a different RTO jurisdiction or in another state from the seller.

faqItems.question: How can I track my vehicle RC transfer application status?
faqItems.answer: Visit the Parivahan Vahan portal and select 'Know Your Application Status' using your 16-digit application number.

GJ.title: How to Transfer Vehicle RC in Gujarat (2026)
GJ.summary: Gujarat Transport Department offers faceless online vehicle ownership transfer via the Parivahan Vahan portal. If transferring from another state, a Gujarat road tax clearance and Form 28 NOC are mandatory.
